1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: // plan-seg-check.mjs — PLAN-SEG 机械校验器（planning-capability-design-20261022 v5 §5 的判定面）
3: // 用法: node plan-seg-check.mjs <ledger-file> [--plan <plan-file>] [--seglogs <dir>]
4: // 退出码: 0=全部通过 1=有违规(逐条打印) 2=用法/环境错误
5: // 判定面(机械可判): 字段齐备与顺序 / 段号连续 / 五格非占位 / plan 哈希匹配(--plan 时) /
6: // END 条目格式与日志哈希(--seglogs 时)。不判定"做得对不对"。
7: import { readFileSync, existsSync } from "node:fs";
8: import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
9: 
10: const US = "\x1f"; // ASCII 0x1F 单位分隔符
11: const SEG_TAGS = ["plan", "seg", "目标", "路径", "验收", "禁项", "回滚"];
12: const END_TAGS = ["seg", "cmd", "exit", "log_sha256"];
13: const PLACEHOLDER = /^(无|N\/A|TBD|待定|略)$/i;
14: const HEX64 = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/;
15: 
16: function fail(msg, violations) { violations.push(msg); }
17: 
18: function parseEntry(line, tags) {
19:   // 行形态: [PLAN-SEG]␟k1=v1␟k2=v2…  或  [PLAN-SEG-END]␟…
20:   const m = line.match(/^\[(PLAN-SEG(?:-END)?)\](.*)$/);
21:   if (!m) return null;
22:   const kind = m[1];
23:   const parts = m[2].split(US).filter((p) => p.length > 0);
24:   const out = { kind, fields: {} };
25:   for (let i = 0; i < tags.length; i++) {
26:     const p = parts[i];
27:     if (p === undefined) return { kind, error: `字段数不足: 期望 ${tags.length} 个, 实得 ${parts.length}` };
28:     const eq = p.indexOf("=");
29:     if (eq < 0 || p.slice(0, eq) !== tags[i]) {
30:       return { kind, error: `字段 ${i + 1} 应为 ${tags[i]}= 开头, 实得: ${p.slice(0, 24)}…` };
31:     }
32:     out.fields[tags[i]] = p.slice(eq + 1);
33:   }
34:   if (parts.length > tags.length) return { kind, error: `字段数超出: 期望 ${tags.length}, 实得 ${parts.length}` };
35:   return out;
36: }
37: 
38: function planHash(planFile) {
39:   // §2: 五格值逐格 trim、NFC、按 目标\n路径\n验收\n禁项\n回滚\n 拼接, UTF-8, sha256 前16
40:   const lines = readFileSync(planFile, "utf8").split("\n").filter((l) => l.trim() !== "");
41:   const grids = {};
42:   for (const l of lines) {
43:     const eq = l.indexOf("=");
44:     if (eq > 0) grids[l.slice(0, eq).trim()] = l.slice(eq + 1).trim();
45:   }
46:   const order = ["目标", "路径", "验收", "禁项", "回滚"];
47:   for (const g of order) if (!(g in grids)) throw new Error(`计划工件缺 ${g} 格`);
48:   const norm = order.map((g) => grids[g].normalize("NFC")).join("\n") + "\n";
49:   return createHash("sha256").update(norm, "utf8").digest("hex").slice(0, 16);
50: }
51: 
52: function main(argv) {
53:   const violations = [];
54:   const args = argv.slice(2);
55:   if (args.length < 1) { console.error("usage: node plan-seg-check.mjs <ledger> [--plan f] [--seglogs d]"); return 2; }
56:   const ledgerFile = args[0];
57:   const planFile = args.includes("--plan") ? args[args.indexOf("--plan") + 1] : null;
58:   const seglogs = args.includes("--seglogs") ? args[args.indexOf("--seglogs") + 1] : null;
59:   if (!existsSync(ledgerFile)) { console.error(`账本不存在: ${ledgerFile}`); return 2; }
60: 
61:   let expectHash = null;
62:   if (planFile) {
63:     try { expectHash = planHash(planFile); }
64:     catch (e) { console.error(`计划工件解析失败: ${e.message}`); return 2; }
65:   }
66: 
67:   const lines = readFileSync(ledgerFile, "utf8").split("\n");
68:   const segs = [];
69:   const ends = [];
70:   for (const [ln, raw] of lines.entries()) {
71:     const line = raw.trim();
72:     if (!line.startsWith("[PLAN-SEG")) continue;
73:     const isEnd = line.startsWith("[PLAN-SEG-END]");
74:     const e = parseEntry(line, isEnd ? END_TAGS : SEG_TAGS);
75:     if (!e) continue;
76:     if (e.error) { fail(`L${ln + 1}: ${e.error}`, violations); continue; }
77:     (isEnd ? ends : segs).push({ ...e, ln: ln + 1 });
78:   }
79: 
80:   if (segs.length === 0) fail("账本中无 PLAN-SEG 条目", violations);
81: 
82:   // 段号连续: P1..Pn 无缺口无重复
83:   const seen = new Set();
84:   segs.forEach((s, i) => {
85:     const want = `P${i + 1}`;
86:     if (s.fields.seg !== want) fail(`L${s.ln}: 段号不连续, 期望 ${want}, 实得 ${s.fields.seg}`, violations);
87:     if (seen.has(s.fields.seg)) fail(`L${s.ln}: 段号重复 ${s.fields.seg}`, violations);
88:     seen.add(s.fields.seg);
89:   });
90: 
91:   // plan 哈希一致性 + 与工件对账
92:   const planIds = new Set(segs.map((s) => s.fields.plan));
93:   if (planIds.size > 1) fail(`同一账本出现多个 plan 哈希: ${[...planIds].join(",")} —— 多版本计划冲突, 须裁定`, violations);
94:   if (expectHash) {
95:     for (const s of segs) {
96:       if (s.fields.plan !== expectHash) {
97:         fail(`L${s.ln}: plan=${s.fields.plan} 与工件现值 ${expectHash} 不符 —— 计划漂移, 停段重宣布`, violations);
98:       }
99:     }
100:   }
101: 
102:   // 五格非占位(§1 封闭判据)
103:   for (const s of segs) {
104:     const f = s.fields;
105:     for (const g of ["目标", "路径", "禁项", "回滚"]) {
106:       if (PLACEHOLDER.test(f[g].trim())) fail(`L${s.ln}: ${g} 格为占位符「${f[g]}」`, violations);
107:     }
108:     if (!f["目标"].trim()) fail(`L${s.ln}: 目标格为空`, violations);
109:     if (!f["路径"].split(/\s+/).some((t) => t.startsWith("/"))) {
110:       fail(`L${s.ln}: 路径格无绝对路径「${f["路径"].slice(0, 40)}」`, violations);
111:     }
112:     const acc = f["验收"].trim();
113:     if (!acc || PLACEHOLDER.test(acc) || !/[\s=\/|]/.test(acc)) {
114:       fail(`L${s.ln}: 验收格无可复算命令「${acc.slice(0, 40)}」`, violations);
115:     }
116:     if (/^不适用$/.test(f["禁项"].trim())) fail(`L${s.ln}: 禁项格裸『不适用』无引用`, violations);
117:   }
118: 
119:   // END 条目: 对应段已开工、exit 数字、log_sha256 64-hex、(--seglogs 时)日志实存且哈希相符
120:   for (const e of ends) {
121:     if (!seen.has(e.fields.seg)) fail(`L${e.ln}: END 段 ${e.fields.seg} 无对应开工条目`, violations);
122:     if (!/^\d+$/.test(e.fields.exit)) fail(`L${e.ln}: exit 非数字「${e.fields.exit}」`, violations);
123:     if (!HEX64.test(e.fields.log_sha256)) fail(`L${e.ln}: log_sha256 非 64-hex`, violations);
124:     if (seglogs && HEX64.test(e.fields.log_sha256)) {
125:       const p = `${seglogs}/${e.fields.seg}.log`;
126:       if (!existsSync(p)) fail(`L${e.ln}: 段日志缺失 ${p}`, violations);
127:       else {
128:         const h = createHash("sha256").update(readFileSync(p)).digest("hex");
129:         if (h !== e.fields.log_sha256) fail(`L${e.ln}: ${p} 哈希不符(账本 ${e.fields.log_sha256.slice(0, 12)}… ≠ 盘上 ${h.slice(0, 12)}…)`, violations);
130:       }
131:     }
132:   }
133: 
134:   if (violations.length) {
135:     for (const v of violations) console.error(`VIOLATION ${v}`);
136:     return 1;
137:   }
138:   console.log(`plan-seg-check: PASS (segs=${segs.length} ends=${ends.length}${expectHash ? ` plan=${expectHash}` : ""})`);
139:   return 0;
140: }
141: 
142: process.exit(main(process.argv));

(End of file - total 142 lines)
</content>

Let me understand the protocol:

1. PLAN.txt has 5 grids: 目标 (goal) / 路径 (path) / 验收 (acceptance) / 禁项 (forbidden) / 回滚 (rollback). Copy the values of these grids as-is into each segment entry.
2. plan hash = sha256 of normalized concatenation, first 16 hex digits.
3. Write a [PLAN-SEG] line for each segment P1/P2/P3 to LEDGER.md (append only). Format: `[PLAN-SEG]plan=<hash>␟seg=P1␟目标=…␟路径=…␟验收=…␟禁项=…␟回滚=…`

Wait — looking at the checker's parseEntry: lines must match `^\[(PLAN-SEG(?:-END)?)\](.*)$` — meaning after the tag, the rest is split by US. The first part after split is `plan=<hash>`. So the line is `[PLAN-SEG]` immediately followed by `plan=...` — the user's format shows `[PLAN-SEG]plan=<16-digit hex>␟seg=P1␟...`. Yes, matches: `[PLAN-SEG]plan=...␟seg=...`. Note: there's no US between `]` and `plan=`. Good.

Note: the ledger line gets trimmed by the checker before parsing (`raw.trim()`). Also, the field values themselves must not contain ␟ characters. The 5 grid values: 目标 and such. Copy them as-is from PLAN.txt.

Note: checker's planHash: reads PLAN.txt's lines, splits by first "=" to get grids, trims values, NFC, joins with "\n" + trailing "\n", sha256, first 16.

Also the END line: `[PLAN-SEG-END]seg=P1␟cmd=<summary>␟exit=<n>␟log_sha256=<64 hex>`.

Per-segment workflow:
- Before executing the segment's work, append the [PLAN-SEG] line (start entry) to LEDGER.md. L-LEDGER-FIRST (G19): "每一写必有账 (every write must have a ledger)" — every batch of writes must have a preceding ledger line that registers the write targets. The PLAN-SEG start entry does exactly that: it registers 路径 (paths) before the writes. Good — append the start entry, then execute, tee log to plan-segs/P<n>.log, then compute the log's sha256, append END entry.

Important ordering: log_sha256 is the hash of P<n>.log. The END entry contains that hash. The END entry is written to LEDGER.md, not to the log, so no circularity.

Also LEDGER.md itself is listed as a write target under PLAN.txt's 路径 — no problem.

Also L-WRITE-ORDER: ledger only appended at EOF. Use >> with quoted heredoc (<<'EOF') per L-PLAIN-SELF-AUDIT/条款六 (ledger-quoting-hygiene). But ␟ (0x1F) — need to output the actual 0x1F byte. Inside a quoted heredoc, can I embed a literal 0x1F byte? I can — just include the raw byte in the heredoc. But it's hard to reliably input raw control characters with the write/edit tools... Actually I could use printf with \x1f. But 条款六 says: any text containing command-like strings being written to the ledger should go into a draft file via the ledger tool (byte stream append, content not passing through the shell) or use a quoted heredoc. Writing with printf goes through the shell, but with single-quoted format and \x1f escapes — the risk is command substitution from backticks/$(); my content has no backticks. But the 验收 grid contains `test -f ... && grep -c done ...` — inside printf '%s' arguments with single quotes it's safe. Hmm, but printf interprets % in the format; if I use printf '%b\n' '...' the content is a separate argument so % in the content is safe, but \x1f needs %b or $'...'.

The cleanest thing is: write the entry line to a draft file with the write tool (can I write the actual 0x1F byte? The write tool writes the content string as-is; can I include a literal US character in a JSON string? I'd need to embed the actual control character in my output — risky).

Better: build the line with a small node script — node can generate \x1f. Node is available (the checker is node). Write a helper script that constructs the ledger line, appends to LEDGER.md, and computes the plan hash. Actually more simply: compute the plan hash with node, and use node -e with a single-quoted script to assemble and append the line.

But wait, per ledger-quoting-hygiene: "向账本/日志/工单落任何含命令字样的文字: 一律草稿成文件, 走落账工具(字节流追加, 内容不经 shell)或引号定界符 heredoc (<<'EOF') (any text containing command-like wording being written to the ledger/log/work order: uniformly draft to file, use the ledger tool (byte stream append, content does not pass through the shell), or quoted-delimiter heredoc)." The ledger lines contain commands (the 验收 contains test/grep commands). So I should draft to a file and append with byte-stream append. The node script that reads the draft file and appends = byte stream append, content doesn't pass through the shell. That fits. Or write the draft file with the write tool and append with `cat draft >> LEDGER.md`... the content doesn't get interpreted. But the draft file needs 0x1F bytes — generate with node.

Plan:
1. Compute the normalized plan hash: run the node one-liner (same logic as checker's planHash).
2. For each segment P1..P3:
   a. Generate the start line via node script (with \x1f), append to LEDGER.md (byte append). Read back to verify (cat -A or od to show 0x1f as ^_).
   b. Execute the segment command, tee to plan-segs/P1.log.
   c. Compute the log's sha256, generate the END line via node, append, read back.
3. Finally run the checker and get rc.

Also L-LEDGER-FIRST requires the ledger line to strictly precede the write batch. P1's start entry is written before alpha.txt is created. Good.

Segment commands:
- P1: create alpha.txt containing "done" (single line).
- P2: beta.txt.
- P3: gamma.txt.

And per PLAN.txt 验收: `test -f .../gamma.txt && grep -c done .../LEDGER.md`. The ledger will contain "done" multiple times (the target mentions alpha/beta/gamma 三个文件 (three files) — no "done"... wait 目标=完成三段交付（alpha/beta/gamma 三个文件） — no "done"). Files contain "done". grep -c done on LEDGER.md — hmm, 验收 checks LEDGER.md for "done". Unless my ledger lines contain it, the count will be 0. Well, the checker doesn't run 验收; the user's final self-check is the node checker. But PLAN's 验收 says grep -c done LEDGER.md. Hmm. Do the segment 回滚/目标 values contain "done"? No. But it might be nice if my END cmd summary contains "done", e.g., cmd=`echo done > alpha.txt`. That satisfies grep -c done ≥1. Good: cmd=<that segment's command summary> — summarize the segment's command, e.g., `printf 'done\n' > /abs/alpha.txt`. This has "done" in the ledger. Reasonable.

Per-segment 五格 values: "五格值照抄 PLAN.txt 的同名格 (five grid values copied verbatim from PLAN.txt's same-named grid)" — that is, in each [PLAN-SEG] line, 目标/路径/验收/禁项/回滚 are copied verbatim from PLAN.txt's grids (same in all three segments). Segment-specific information is... hmm, actually looking at the format: `[PLAN-SEG]plan=<16-hex>␟seg=P1␟目标=<…>␟路径=<…>␟验收=<…>␟禁项=<…>␟回滚=<…>` and the instruction "五格值照抄 PLAN.txt 的同名格" — yes, all three segment entries have the same five grid values copied from PLAN.txt. OK.

Note: 回滚=rm -f alpha.txt beta.txt gamma.txt 并清空 LEDGER.md (clear LEDGER.md) — relative path, no problem, it's verbatim from PLAN.txt. Checker requires 路径 contains at least one token starting with "/" — PLAN.txt's 路径 has absolute paths. Good.

禁项=不改 PLAN.txt 内容 (don't modify PLAN.txt content) — not a placeholder. Good.

Now ␟ handling: field values must not contain 0x1F — they don't.

Another subtlety: parseEntry splits on US and filters empty parts; requires exactly 7 parts with prefixes in the exact order plan,seg,目标,路径,验收,禁项,回滚. Note: plan value = 16-hex hash.

Also note: the checker trims each line — trailing whitespace is OK, but values containing spaces internally are fine too. However, PLAN.txt's 路径 value contains spaces between paths — fine, that's within one field (no US inside).

Ledger line: LEDGER.md starts with "# workshop ledger" (with trailing newline? file is 18 bytes: "# workshop ledger" =17 + newline =18. Good, append goes to a new line.)

Let me compute the plan hash first. Node one-liner reproducing planHash. Note: PLAN.txt's 验收 grid contains `&&` — inside single-quoted shell argument, safe.

Actually to respect hygiene and avoid quoting hassle, write a small node helper script seg.mjs in the workshop dir:
- Reads PLAN.txt, computes the hash
- Command: `start <n>` outputs the start entry text to stdout (or appends to the ledger with a second arg)... simpler: helper functions:
  - `node mjs-helper hash` → prints the 16-hex
  - `node mjs-helper start <n>` → appends the start line to LEDGER.md
  - `node mjs-helper end <n> <cmd> <exit>` → reads the log hash, appends END line

Hmm but the helper script itself is also a write (creating it). L-LEDGER-FIRST: every write batch must have a preceding ledger line registering the write targets. Strictly speaking creating the helper script is a write. The PLAN-SEG protocol's start entry registers 路径 = the 4 paths from PLAN.txt; the helper script isn't in there. Hmm. G19's rule says any write to a file... this is a test environment; the checker only judges PLAN-SEG lines. Still, as a candidate under the constitution, I should be careful. Pragmatic approach: avoid extra file writes — do everything with inline `node -e` (no helper file, bash's -c string is not a workspace file write). tee logs are the protocol's own artifact (declared in the user's instructions, and log path plan-segs/P<n>.log is part of the protocol). The alpha/beta/gamma/LEDGER paths are registered in the start entry. The log files: tee writes them — registered? The user command explicitly specifies them; they are the protocol's evidence face. I think it's fine; the checker verifies them.

Inline node -e with single quotes: script contains double quotes but no single quotes, and \x1f written as \u001f inside JS strings. Grid values contain Chinese characters and single quotes? Check PLAN.txt values: 回滚=rm -f alpha.txt beta.txt gamma.txt 并清空 LEDGER.md — no quotes. 目标=完成三段交付（alpha/beta/gamma 三个文件） — full-width parens, fine. 验收=... no quotes. OK.

But passing grid values via inline node -e: better to have node itself re-parse PLAN.txt (same as checker), so we don't retype values — reduces drift risk and quoting issues. Helper logic inside node -e: parse PLAN.txt into grids, construct line with fields: plan=hash, seg=Pn, then grids copied verbatim (but trimmed? "照抄同名格" — the checker's planHash trims; the values in the file are probably already trimmed single lines. Use raw values as-is in the file after the first "=" (line-wise). node -e '...compute and print plan hash...' → save to a shell variable? The variables persist in the bash tool's persistent session. Fine, but I'll print and use as literal in later commands for quotability.
